samanta-b06-03: Use case: illustration-story. Original literary pen-line book vignette for proverb 'Dig a mountain; kill a mouse', emphasizing huge effort versus tiny result. A broad rocky mound has an oversized excavated opening, with two simple digging tools resting beside it; a very small live mouse sits unharmed at the opening. Clear comic scale contrast, no dead animal, blood or violence, no miners or machinery, no geological claim. Imagined metaphor. Fine black hand-drawn outlines, sparse hatching, no colour, no large filled black tunnel, white background, no text or border, generous margins, compact square illustration readable at small book size.
samanta-b06-15: Use case: illustration-story. Original small literary pen-and-ink vignette for an Odia saying satirizing authority being accepted because of who speaks. Use a clearly imagined contemporary analogy, not a literal depiction of Brahma or sacred scripture: a confident adult speaker at a plain lectern gestures vaguely while two seated adult listeners exchange puzzled glances, one holding a blank notebook. No text, speech bubbles, religious objects, political symbols, portraits of real people or mocking caricature. Natural varied posture, believable hands and sightlines; mild humour in the listeners' uncertainty. Fine black outlines and sparse hatching, pure white background, no colour, no heavy shadows, no border, generous margins and compact square book-vignette composition.
